title: Coherent generators and a morphism criterion for finite-cover sites
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention] whose category has finite limits and whose topology is generated by a pretopology consisting of finite covering families. Write $\mathcal E=\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ and $H_U=h_U^\#$ for the sheafification of the representable presheaf of an object $U$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Each $H_U$ is a coherent object in the sense of [def-trf-coherent-topos], and these objects form a generating family whose closure under finite limits in $\mathcal E$ consists of coherent objects. In particular $\mathcal E$ is a coherent topos. If $\mathcal E'$ is any coherent topos and $u:\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E$ is a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] such that $u^{-1}H_U$ is coherent for every $U\in\mathcal C$, then $u^{-1}$ takes every coherent object of $\mathcal E$ to a coherent object of $\mathcal E'$, so $u$ is coherent.

source.place: §8.1, printed p. 17: the finite-cover-site coherence criterion and preservation of coherent objects used for the triple sites. The same criterion is used in literature/illusie-laszlo-orgogozo-travaux-de-gabber_arXiv-1207.3648.pdf, Exposé XI, proof of Lemma 2.5, printed pp. 178–179 (PDF pp. 184–185). This node states the abstract criterion, not its oriented-product application.

proof.text: Set $I=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $G_U=H_U$. By [lem-trf-finitary-representable-pullback-charts], this is a small quasi-compact generating family, $G_1\simeq1$ and $G_V\times G_W\simeq G_{V\times W}$. For every $U,V,W$ and every pair of sheaf arrows $G_V\to G_U$, $G_W\to G_U$, the same node gives a quasi-compact pullback; no global site-arrow representatives are required. These are exactly the generating-family, terminal, product and arbitrary-arrow pullback hypotheses of [lem-trf-coherent-generator-subobject-closure]. Its conclusions give coherence of each $H_U$ and of every object in their finite-limit closure, and a small full generating subcategory of coherent objects closed under finite limits. This is coherence of $\mathcal E$ by [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: Assembly of the finite-chart and coherent-subobject closure lemmas, expanding the finite-cover criterion used in Exposé XI, proof of Lemma 2.5.

proof.text: For any coherent $A$, put $L=u^{-1}$ and use the small-site sheaf presentation of $\mathcal E'$ supplied by [def-trf-coherent-topos]. By [def-trf-geometric-morphism], $L$ is a left exact left adjoint between these sheaf categories. Apply [lem-trf-left-exact-finite-relation-presentation] to the small quasi-compact generating family $(H_U)$ established in step 1 and the assumed coherence of each $LH_U$. It gives an epimorphism $Lp:LP\to LA$ with $LP$ coherent and kernel pair $LR\simeq LP\times_{LA}LP$ quasi-compact, compatible with both projections. Finite coherent sums use [lem-trf-sheaf-quasicompact-coproduct-calculus]; quasi-compact sums and epic images use [lem-trf-topos-finite-cover-calculus], both including empty families. The target topos is coherent by hypothesis, so [lem-trf-coherent-epimorphic-quotient] applies to $Lp$ and proves $LA$ coherent. This holds for every coherent $A$, which is exactly coherence of $u$ [def-trf-coherent-topos].

source.place: Assembly of finite object-and-relation transport, quasi-compactness calculus, and coherent epimorphic quotient criterion.
